# Flyout

Header: `winui/ui/dialogs/Flyout.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/dialogs/Flyout.hpp`.

Arbitrary content floating in a popup next to an owned anchor.

The content sits on a surface with the theme's elevated menu background and a 1 DIP frame. The padding is 16, 15, 16 and 17 DIPs (left, top, right, bottom). The surface is at least 96x40 and at most 456x758 DIPs, so long text wraps at 456. Opening, placement and focus work as in [FlyoutBase](#class-flyoutbase). A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor opens it on click, and any other anchor on a click nothing inside it handled.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
ui::ObservableVector<std::string> cart;
ui::Control<ui::Flyout>           flyout;
window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
    .placement = ui::PopupPlacement::Right,
    .control   = flyout,
    .anchor    = ui::Button{.text = "Empty cart"},
    .content   = ui::VerticalStack{
        .spacing  = 12.0f,
        .content  = {
            ui::Text{.text = "All items will be removed. Continue?"},
            ui::Button{.text = "Yes, empty my cart", .on_click = [&] { cart.clear(); flyout->hide(); }},
        },
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto owned = std::make_unique<ui::FlyoutControl>();
owned->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Open"));
owned->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Flyout content"));
stack->add(std::move(owned));
```

## `ui::Flyout`

An anchor element with content that floats above the tree when opened. Builds a [ui::FlyoutControl](#uiflyoutcontrol). A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor opens it on click, Enter or Space by itself. Any other anchor opens it on a click that nothing inside it handled, by pointer only. From code, call show() on the control from [`.control`](#uiflyout-control). It opens below the anchor, and an outside click or Escape closes it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ObservableVector<std::string> cart;
ui::Control<ui::Flyout>           confirm;

window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
    .control = confirm,
    .anchor  = ui::Button{ .text = "Empty cart" },
    .content = ui::VerticalStack{
        .spacing  = 12,
        .content  = {
            ui::Text{ .text = "All items will be removed. Do you want to continue?" },
            ui::Button{ .text = "Yes, empty my cart", .on_click = [&] { cart.clear(); confirm->hide(); } },
        },
    },
});
```

```cpp
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_opened, .on_closing,
    .on_closed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .anchor, .content
}
```

| <span id="uiflyout-placement"></span>`placement` | `ui::Binding<ui::PopupPlacement>` | `{ui::PopupPlacement::Below}` | Which side of the anchor it opens on; PopupPlacement::Below by default. |
| <span id="uiflyout-placement_alignment"></span>`placement_alignment` | `ui::Binding<ui::PopupPlacementAlignment>` | `{ui::PopupPlacementAlignment::Center}` | How the flyout lines up with the anchor along that side. |
| <span id="uiflyout-show_mode"></span>`show_mode` | `ui::Binding<ui::FlyoutShowMode>` | `{ui::FlyoutShowMode::Standard}` | Standard takes keyboard focus while open, Transient leaves it where it is. |
| <span id="uiflyout-light_dismiss"></span>`light_dismiss` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{true}` | Whether an outside click or Escape closes it; true by default. Off, it stays open until [`is_open`](#uiflyout-is_open) turns false, hide() runs or a command in it runs. |

| <span id="uiflyout-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Flyout>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Arbitrary content floating in a popup next to an owned anchor.

The content sits on a surface with the theme's elevated menu background and a 1 DIP frame. The padding is 16, 15, 16 and 17 DIPs (left, top, right, bottom). The surface is at least 96x40 and at most 456x758 DIPs, so long text wraps at 456. Opening, placement and focus work as in [FlyoutBase](#class-flyoutbase). A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor opens it on click, and any other anchor on a click nothing inside it handled.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:

window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
```


Takes ownership of the floating content, replacing any previous one, and returns a non-owning observer. The content shows while [is_open()](#is_open). It is not part of the main tree. The window lays it out and draws it separately, in its popup layer.

## class FlyoutBase

Derives from `ui::Element`.

What every flyout shares: an owned anchor element it opens from, opening and closing, placement against the anchor or at a point, focus handling, and the open and close fade.

A [FlyoutBase](#class-flyoutbase) wraps its anchor. [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout), rendering, input, focus and automation pass through to the anchor, and the flyout manages the popup. A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor opens the flyout on click and with Enter or Space by itself ([ButtonControl::set_flyout()](button.md#set_flyout)). Any other anchor opens it on a left click that nothing inside the anchor handled. So a [Text](text.md#uitext), an [Image](image.md#uiimage) or a card opens it by pointer, while a [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox) or a [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) inside still does only its own thing. Such an anchor has no keyboard shortcut to open it, so call [show()](#show) or [toggle()](#toggle) from its own handler for that.

By default the popup opens below the anchor, centered and 4 DIPs away from it, and flips when there is no room. [show_at()](#show_at) puts its top-left corner at a point instead, as a context menu does. [FlyoutBase](#class-flyoutbase) can't be constructed directly. Use [Flyout](#uiflyout), [MenuFlyout](menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout) or [CommandBarFlyout](command-bar-flyout.md#uicommandbarflyout).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  flyout = std::make_unique<ui::FlyoutControl>();
flyout->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Options")); // clicks toggle the flyout
flyout->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Hello"));
flyout->set_placement(ui::PopupPlacement::Above);
flyout->set_placement_alignment(ui::PopupPlacementAlignment::Leading);
flyout->on_closed([](ui::PopupCloseReason) { std::println("flyout closed"); });
window.set_content(std::move(flyout));
```

### set_anchor

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_anchor(std::unique_ptr<T> anchor)
```

Takes ownership of the anchor element, replacing any previous one, and returns a non-owning observer, as [ScrollControl::set_child()](../layout/scroll.md#set_child) does. A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor toggles the flyout on click.

### anchor

```cpp
Element* anchor() const
```

The anchor element (non-owning), or nullptr.

### is_open

```cpp
bool is_open() const
```

True while the flyout is shown or fading in. It turns false as soon as [hide()](#hide), an outside click or Escape commits to closing, though the popup keeps drawing while it fades out ([transition_opacity()](#transition_opacity)).

### show

```cpp
void show()
```

Opens the flyout against the anchor, on the side [placement()](#placement) names, and raises [on_opened()](#on_opened). Does nothing while already open.

### show_at

```cpp
void show_at(Point point)
```

Opens the flyout with its top-left corner at `point` (window-client DIPs), as a context menu opens at the pointer.

### hide

```cpp
void hide()
```

Closes with PopupCloseReason::Programmatic. [on_closing()](#on_closing) can cancel it. Otherwise the close fade starts, [is_open()](#is_open) turns false at once, and [on_closed()](#on_closed) runs once the fade ends. Does nothing while already closed.

### toggle

```cpp
void toggle()
```

[hide()](#hide) when open, [show()](#show) otherwise.

### placement

```cpp

```

Which side of the anchor the content opens against; PopupPlacement::Below by default. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room.

### set_placement

```cpp
void set_placement(PopupPlacement placement)
```

Sets the side; applies the next time the popup is placed.

### placement_alignment

```cpp
PopupPlacementAlignment placement_alignment() const
```

The alignment across the placement axis; Center by default.

### set_placement_alignment

```cpp
void set_placement_alignment(PopupPlacementAlignment alignment)
```

Sets the alignment across the placement axis.


Whether an open flyout takes keyboard focus; Standard (it does) by default.

### set_show_mode

```cpp
void set_show_mode(FlyoutShowMode mode)
```

Sets whether the next open takes keyboard focus.

### light_dismiss

```cpp
bool light_dismiss() const
```

Whether an outside click or Escape closes the flyout; true by default. Off, it stays open until [hide()](#hide) or a command in it closes it, and an outside click reaches what is below.

### set_light_dismiss

```cpp
void set_light_dismiss(bool enabled)
```

Turns light dismiss on or off.

### on_opened

```cpp
void on_opened(Callback<void()> handler)
```

Raised when [show()](#show) or [show_at()](#show_at) opens the flyout.

### on_closing

```cpp
void on_closing(Callback<Decision(const PopupClosingArgs&)> handler)
```

Raised with the reason before an open flyout closes; return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it open.

### on_closed

```cpp
void on_closed(Callback<void(PopupCloseReason)> handler)
```

Raised with the reason once the flyout has closed and its close fade has finished (not when [on_closing()](#on_closing) canceled). The handler may destroy the flyout.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Whether this element can take keyboard focus (a leaf control opts in).

### handle_global_shortcut

```cpp
bool handle_global_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

The shortcuts that fire wherever focus is. The ones a command surface carries are of this kind (a [MenuBar](menu-bar.md#uimenubar)'s Ctrl+S, a [MenuFlyout](menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout) item's Delete, an [AppBarButton](app-bar-button.md#uiappbarbutton)'s Ctrl+N), so those controls answer here. [Window](../tree/window.md) offers a key that no scoped shortcut took to every element in the window, in tree order, when the focused element and its parents did not handle the key themselves ([key_override()](#key_override)). Default: none.

### raise_context_requested

```cpp
bool raise_context_requested(std::optional<Point> position) override
```

A right-click lands on the anchor, though the flyout holds its place in the tab order. The anchor's context request handler runs first, then the flyout's own.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Visits the anchor, if any. The popup is not a child.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

The flyout stands in for its anchor as one tab stop. Focus itself goes to the anchor.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>&) const override
```

No automation children: the anchor is not listed under the flyout.

### transition_opacity

```cpp
float transition_opacity() const override
```

A linear fade over the open and close transitions by default. A plain [Flyout](#uiflyout) has no opening slide.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Passes through to the anchor, like every [Element](../tree/element.md) override above. Screen readers see the anchor, with the open popup's content as its child.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

[automation_name()](../tree/element.md#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

### automation_providers

```cpp
void automation_providers(AutomationProviders& out) override
```

Lists what a client can do with this node: set `out`'s field for each pattern this control implements now to `this`, through the provider interface it inherits privately (ui/Automation.hpp). A pattern that only applies in some states is an `if`. `out` arrives empty, and nothing is listed by default.

Example: 
```cpp
class Chip final : public ui::Element, private ui::InvokeProvider
{
protected:
    void automation_providers(ui::AutomationProviders& out) override
    {
        out.invoke = this;
    }

private:
    bool invoke() override
    {
        on_click_();
        return true;
    }
    ui::Callback<void()> on_click_;
};
```

```cpp
FlyoutBase() = default
```


The current phase, for a derived flyout's rendering. The popup stays open through Closing, so it fades out.

How far the current Opening or Closing transition is, 0 to 1 (1 once Open or Closed).

### set_transition_durations


The open and close transitions' lengths; 250 ms each by default. A derived flyout with its own motion sets them in its constructor.

### positioned_at_point

```cpp
bool positioned_at_point() const
```

Whether the current or last open was [show_at()](#show_at), placed at a point, instead of [show()](#show).

### close

```cpp
void close(PopupCloseReason reason)
```

Closes for `reason`: raises [on_closing()](#on_closing), and unless a handler cancels, starts the close fade. A derived flyout closes with PopupCloseReason::Invoked once a command in it ran.

### opening_override

```cpp
virtual void opening_override()
```

Called as [show()](#show) or [show_at()](#show_at) commits to opening, before the Opening transition starts. Reset the popup's own state here.

### closing_override

```cpp
virtual void closing_override()
```

Called as a close commits, once no [on_closing()](#on_closing) handler canceled it.

### flyout_surface

```cpp
virtual Element* flyout_surface() = 0
```

The element the flyout floats while it shows: its surface, built on first call. Null floats nothing.

### popup_element

```cpp

```

The popup's element, which the flyout ticks and clears of dirty flags itself because it is not in the window's tree. [flyout_surface()](#flyout_surface) by default.

### flyout_chrome

```cpp
virtual void flyout_chrome(PopupChrome& chrome)
```

The shadow the window draws behind the surface; the theme's flyout shadow by default.

### flyout_dismissed

```cpp

```

An outside click or Escape: closes with PopupCloseReason::LightDismiss by default.

### sync_popup

```cpp
void sync_popup()
```

Opens, updates or closes the popup to match the phase, the anchor and the settings. A derived flyout calls it when its surface or chrome changes.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Clears the anchor, and the popup too, which is outside the tree [Window](../tree/window.md) clears.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Ticks the anchor, the popup while it shows, and the open/close transition.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A left click on the anchor that nothing inside it handled opens the flyout while it is closed. Presses on the open popup's content never open it again.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### text_override

```cpp
bool text_override(const TextInputEvent& text_event) override
```

Typed text for this element, routed like [key_override()](#key_override). Default: false.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_visible_changed

```cpp
void focus_visible_changed(bool visible) override
```

[focus_visible()](../tree/element.md#focus_visible) changed; the element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### draws_focus_ring

```cpp
bool draws_focus_ring() const override
```

None of its own: the anchor inside it draws its own focus ring.

## Enumerations

### FlyoutShowMode

```cpp
enum class FlyoutShowMode
```

Whether an open flyout takes keyboard focus.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Standard` | takes keyboard focus while open |
| `Transient` | leaves focus where it is |

### FlyoutPhase

```cpp
enum class FlyoutPhase
```

Where a flyout is in its open and close cycle ([FlyoutBase::phase()](#phase)). During Closing, is_open() is already false, but the popup keeps drawing and fades out until the close transition ends.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Closed` | not shown |
| `Opening` | shown, fading in |
| `Open` | shown |
| `Closing` | committed to closing, fading out |
